notes: Constructor. Second param i is passed straight through to the abstract base CacheEntryReference's constructor param (anInt9545), which LruByteCache.kt treats as a cache-budget cost: it's compared against/subtracted from capacity counters (anInt1084/anInt1086) when entries are inserted or evicted. anObject10429 is the strongly (hard) held cached value, returned verbatim by method3193/get.

Override of abstract CacheEntryReference.method3195. Always returns false, i.e. a hard reference is never soft/never eligible for GC-based eviction - contrast with SoftCacheEntryReference.method3195 which always returns true. Confirmed by LruByteCache usage, e.g. method575: `if (!ref.method3195(-4)) i_0_++` counts non-soft (hard) entries, and method578 branches on this flag to decide whether to demote a hard entry or check-and-purge a cleared soft one. Param i is unused/decoy - callers always pass -4.

Override of abstract CacheEntryReference.method3193. Simply returns the held anObject10429 unconditionally - contrast with SoftCacheEntryReference.method3193 which dereferences a SoftReference and can return null. Param i is unused/decoy here (callers pass varying constants like 86/100/114/119 across LruByteCache call sites, but this override ignores it entirely - only SoftCacheEntryReference's version inspects it, via `if (i <= 75) return null`).
